programmes.programName: Ph.D. in Business Administration with a major in Management Information Systems
programmes.department: Department of Business Analytics, Information Systems and Supply Chain
programmes.evidence: The official MIS doctoral overview explicitly describes research in service and retail operations, with interdisciplinary faculty expertise across operations management, management science and supply chain. The current department page explicitly administers this MIS major with a PhD coordinator, and the central business inventory confirms the Business Administration degree.
limitations: The exact major is MIS, not a separately awarded Operations doctorate. Only its explicitly stated service/retail operations research remit establishes eligible scope.

programmes.department: Department of Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering
programmes.evidence: FSU’s current doctoral inventory explicitly lists Industrial Engineering and links to the joint FAMU-FSU department. The official degree matrix calls its doctorate Industrial Engineering Ph.D.; the doctoral requirements page establishes research, candidacy and dissertation. This is one shared college route, recorded through the verified FSU provider link.
limitations: The requirements prose also calls the doctorate Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering. The actual matrix degree label Industrial Engineering Ph.D. is retained rather than inventing two degrees.
FAMU-FSU College is explicitly shared by Florida A&M and Florida State. University-specific registration/awarding mechanics remain unverified; no separate duplicate FAMU route is created.

programmes.department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering
programmes.evidence: The official joint-college graduate page explicitly defines the Civil Engineering PhD as a research degree with original independent scholarship and dissertation. It directly lists current CEE research fields. The opened Intelligent Mobility and Community Resilience field explicitly establishes smart logistics and optimization, freight logistics, traffic operations, evacuation and shelter capacity allocation research. Candidates may enter through either FAMU or FSU admissions.
limitations: Intelligent Mobility and Logistics is a current doctoral research pathway in the broad Civil degree, not a separately titled degree or formal concentration.

One joint-college route is recorded through the FSU doctoral inventory and explicit FSU admission pathway. FAMU-specific registration/degree-awarding mechanics remain unverified; no duplicate route is created.
